sample.author: Jérôme Respaut
sample.subject: feat(SREAA-368): upgrade module to v9 (OpenTofu >= 1.12, AzureRM ~> 5.0)
sample.body:
Align the module with the v9 baseline of the Claranet Azure module collection and
migrate the Storage Account code to the AzureRM 5.0 schema.

* Require OpenTofu `>= 1.12` in `versions.tofu`
* Bump the AzureRM provider constraint to `~> 5.0`
* Bump the `azurecaf` provider constraint to `~> 1.3.0`
* Bump the `claranet/diagnostic-settings/azurerm` module calls to `~> 9.0`
* Update `TF_MIN_VERSION` and `AZURERM_PROVIDER_MIN_VERSION` in `.gitlab-ci.yml`
* Apply the same OpenTofu and AzureRM constraints to the three `examples/`
* Sync `.config/terraform-docs.yml` and `.config/tflint.hcl` with the `ci` repository
* Refresh `mise.lock` so it matches the tools pinned in `.tool-versions`
* Regenerate `README.md` with `terraform-docs`

AzureRM 5.0 code migration:

* Move the inline `static_website` block of `azurerm_storage_account` to the dedicated
  `azurerm_storage_account_static_website` resource in `r-static-website.tf`, keeping the
  `static_website_config` variable as the module interface and carrying the
  `StorageV2` / `BlockBlobStorage` restriction over as a `precondition`
* Expose the new resource through the `resource_static_website` output
* Replace `storage_account_name` with `storage_account_id` on `azurerm_storage_queue` and
  `azurerm_storage_table`
* Drop `customer_managed_key.managed_hsm_key_id`, removed by the provider, and make
  `key_vault_key_id` mandatory as the provider schema now requires it
* Constrain `min_tls_version` to `TLS1_2` with a validation so rejected values surface at
  plan time instead of apply time

BREAKING CHANGES: the minimum OpenTofu version is raised to `1.12` and the AzureRM
provider is constrained to `~> 5.0`, so consumers must upgrade both before using this
release. Static website settings now live in a separate resource, so consumers already
using `static_website_config` must import it with
`tofu import 'module.<name>.azurerm_storage_account_static_website.main[0]' <storage_account_id>`
before applying, otherwise the plan recreates the configuration. The
`customer_managed_key.managed_hsm_key_id` attribute is gone and Managed HSM keys must be
supplied through `key_vault_key_id`, which is now a required attribute of the
`customer_managed_key` object instead of an optional one. `min_tls_version` no longer
accepts `TLS1_0` or `TLS1_1`. The `diagnostic-settings` submodule moves to `~> 9.0`, which
requires AzureRM `~> 5.0` as well. Two provider-level behaviour changes shipped with
AzureRM 5.0 also apply: `resource_provider_registrations` now defaults to `none` instead of
`legacy`, so no resource provider is registered automatically anymore, and the
`enhanced_validation` block moved inside `features` with location and resource provider
validation now disabled by default, which defers those errors from plan time to apply time.

sample.author: caballeto
sample.subject: fix(monitor): correct status_code assertion docs + orphan-cleanup safety net (#16)
sample.body:
Round-2 DevEx surfaced two issues with `assertions { type = "status_code" }`:

1. **Docs example used `expected = 200`** (number). The API contract is
   `String expected` (so it can carry "200", "2xx", "200-299"), and Jackson
   silently coerces the number to "200" on store. The round-trip then trips
   Terraform's "Provider produced inconsistent result after apply" check
   AND, because the API call had already succeeded by then, leaves an
   orphaned monitor server-side that no Terraform state file references.

   Fix: example now uses `expected = "200"` with an inline comment
   explaining why. Schema description for `assertions[].config` calls out
   the type-strictness rule explicitly (status_code.expected is STRING,
   response_time.thresholdMs is NUMBER).

2. **Create-flow had no orphan rollback.** If `mapToState` or
   `resp.State.Set` failed AFTER the API create, the monitor leaked.

   Fix: thread a `cleanupOrphan` closure through Create and call DELETE
   if either downstream step returns an error. Logged at Debug on success
   and Warn on failure (so the leaked-id is visible to operators in
   either case).

   This does NOT cover the framework's post-Create consistency check
   (which runs after our function returns and is what produced the
   round-2 reports). The fix for that path is the doc/example change
   above — once user values match the API's wire format, the matching
   logic in `mapToState` produces consistent state and the framework
   never errors. The cleanup closure protects against any future
   internal failure in the same window.

Round-2 DevEx friction P0 #1 + P0 #3 (see /tmp/devex-cli-test/FRICTION-TABLE.md).

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

sample.author: caballeto
sample.subject: fix(examples): correct assertion config + status-page branding examples (#4)
sample.body:
The bundled examples and the auto-generated docs site were rendering API
configurations that the platform rejects. A v0.1.0-alpha.4 production smoke
test surfaced four issues, all in copy-paste-ready snippets:

1. status_code assertion missing the required `operator` field. The API has
   required `operator` since March 2026 (StatusCodeAssertion DTO).
2. response_time assertion using snake_case `threshold_ms`. API field names
   inside the assertion `config` JSON are camelCase (`thresholdMs`); the
   Terraform-attribute snake_case convention does not apply inside JSON
   payloads.
3. Status-page `hide_powered_by = true` shown without noting it requires a
   Business plan. Lower tiers receive a 400.
4. Misleading example in MonitorResource schema description for
   `assertions.config` — it showed `expected = 200` (no operator) and
   propagated through tfplugindocs into the public registry docs.

Changes:
- examples/resources/devhelm_monitor/resource.tf: add `operator = "equals"`,
  use `thresholdMs`, add a clarifying comment.
- examples/resources/devhelm_status_page/resource.tf: comment out
  `hide_powered_by` with a plan-tier note.
- internal/provider/resources/monitor.go: fix the schema description
  example so the registry-rendered help text is correct.
- templates/guides/getting-started.md.tmpl: same assertion fixes.
- docs/* regenerated via `make docs`.

The provider code itself is unchanged — these were all hand-authored example
artifacts that were never executed against the API. Fixing the bundled
examples-as-CI gap is a separate follow-up.

sample.author: Alisdair McDiarmid
sample.subject: core: Check rule error message expressions
sample.body:
Error messages for preconditions, postconditions, and custom variable
validations have until now been string literals. This commit changes
this to treat the field as an HCL expression, which must evaluate to a
string. Most commonly this will either be a string literal or a template
expression.

When the check rule condition is evaluated, we also evaluate the error
message. This means that the error message should always evaluate to a
string value, even if the condition passes. If it does not, this will
result in an error diagnostic.

If the condition fails, and the error message also fails to evaluate, we
fall back to a default error message. This means that the check rule
failure will still be reported, alongside diagnostics explaining why the
custom error message failed to render.

As part of this change, we also necessarily remove the heuristic about
the error message format. This guidance can be readded in future as part
of a configuration hint system.

sample.subject: feat: add vpc_cni_env passthrough for VPC CNI addon configuration (#206)
sample.body:
* feat: add vpc_cni_env passthrough for VPC CNI addon configuration

Allows callers to set aws-node env vars (e.g. WARM_IP_TARGET,
MINIMUM_IP_TARGET) without overriding the whole vpc-cni addon entry,
which would drop the module-internal IRSA/pod-identity wiring.

* fix: omit configuration_values key entirely when vpc_cni_env unset

Review feedback: key-present-with-null is not identical to key-absent
for downstream map merges. Also document that vpc_cni_env values land
in plan/state and must not carry secrets.

* feat: configure vpc-cni addon before compute

Applies CNI settings before EC2 nodes launch so first nodes bootstrap
with the intended IPAM configuration (prefix delegation max-pods,
custom networking). Existing consumers see a one-time addon resource
replacement; preserve=true keeps aws-node running through it, or use
terraform state mv to avoid the replacement entirely.
